text:
sam: hitting a weird edge case when using the TS SDK from an ESM-only app on the edge runtime. types blow up with our generic overloads.
maya: ugh, details? repro? :eyes:
sam: minimal repro attached inline — function overloads with generic defaults start resolving to `any` in the bundle on Vercel Edge. works with node CJS. here's simplified:
sam: ```ts
// sdk.ts
export function call<T = unknown>(input: T): Promise<string>;
export function call(input: any) { return Promise.resolve(String(input)); }
```
sam: consuming app (ESM, TS 5.1):
sam: ```ts
import { call } from 'redwood-sdk';
const r = await call({ foo: 1 });
// TS infers r as any, not Promise<string>
```
alex: hmm. could be declaration emit + package.json exports + `types` entry getting messed by our bundler. Do you build .d.ts into dist? maya: we do, but tsc + rollup combo sometimes rewrites path mappings. build-bot: CI warning: "warning TS7031: Binding element 'T' implicitly has an 'any' type." on esm build job.
jordan: also check tsconfig `module`/`moduleResolution`. edge bundlers (Vite/Rspack) often use `bundler` resolution which affects fallback to declaration files.
sam: tried forcing `skipLibCheck: true` + `declaration: true` and still flaky. locally `tsc --build` gives correct types, but after our publish step (tsup -> cjs+esm) consumers see wrong inference.
maya: could it be that our .d.ts for overloaded functions gets flattened by tsup? I remember tsup has `dts` plugin that collapses overload signatures.
alex: yep. dts bundlers often output a single implementation signature which loses distinct overloads/generic defaults. Solution options:
- emit unbundled `.d.ts` files (preserve per-file declarations)
- add a manually authored `index.d.ts` that re-exports the proper overloads
- change to single generic signature that preserves inference (but that's API change)
sam: unbundled d.ts seems safest for parity. any downsides? jordan: increases package size slightly, but typings are tiny. main friction: our publish tooling needs to copy `dist/types` and ensure package.json `types` points to dist/types/index.d.ts.
maya: also check package.json `exports` field — if we export `./package.json` or have conditional exports that point to dist/esm/index.js but types to dist/index.d.ts, some bundlers might not pick it up. recommended pattern:

```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts"
  }
}
```

(not all bundlers support types in exports, so we should still have top-level "types" field)
alex: action: let's stop collapsing declarations in tsup. @alex I'll open a PR to switch tsup dts config to emit per-file declarations and add a publish step that copies `dist/types`. @maya can you add a smoke test: a tiny ESM edge app in examples that imports the SDK and checks inferred types via a TS compile step in CI? maya: will do.
sam: repro for CI: put a tiny sample under examples/edge-typing-smoke and run `tsc --noEmit` in GH actions using Node 20 + tsc from dev deps.
jordan: also include a note in docs: "If you use ESM edge runtimes, prefer unbundled type files or pin TS versions to >=5.0". add a tip about `moduleResolution: bundler` causing differences.
build-bot: created issue #4123: "ESM build: overloads lost in bundled d.ts -> consumer inference broken" assigned to alex.
alex: PR opened: #4124 switching tsup dts mode + adding examples smoke test. I'll ping for review when green. :rocket:
sam: thanks all — after PR lands I'll try on the Vercel project. will report back.
